question.text: Sahyadri Stat-Arb Fund, a Cat III AIF, wants to add a commodity-futures sleeve to its playbook. Per Section 2.6.1 (citing SEBI Circulars dated June 21, 2017 and September 29, 2017), what is the MAXIMUM percentage of investable funds a Cat III AIF may commit to ONE underlying commodity on the commodity-derivatives exchanges?

answer.text: There is no cap - Cat III is free to concentrate in a single commodity

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 2.6.1 states: "Indian Category III AIFs are permitted by SEBI to invest in all commodity derivatives products that are being traded on the commodity derivatives exchanges. They can invest up to 10 percent of the investable funds in one underlying commodity, subject to the reporting requirements set forth by SEBI" (SEBI Circulars of 21-Jun-2017 and 29-Sep-2017). The single-commodity cap is therefore 10%. The Trap: Option A (5%) undershoots the circular limit. Option C (25%) is not the single-commodity figure. Option D ignores that even Category III is subject to prudential concentration caps. Note: The Category III investment-condition page (pp. 47, 404) sets a 10% single-investee limit generally and 20% for large value funds for accredited investors - distinct from the 10% single-commodity cap in this question. The two limits should not be conflated.
